column5: Building a harmonized regime is not working, so we can forget that. Building a new regime, a 28th one, is an option, but it is not the only one. An equivalent, though much cheaper solution would be to let firms choose among existing (27) regimes. Luxembourg as EU Delaware?

column11: ESMA is the wrong institution to pick for a European SEC. It is set up as a democratic, college-like regulator rather than a technical supervisory team, but rather representatives of their respective. governments. We desperately need an. independent and competent authority.

column5: Time is now of the essence. There is considerable evidence that EU harmonization of rules is slow and not very effective. EU harmonization with national implementation can even increase differences across EU markets (see link below).

column11: National regulatory agencies differ in capabilities, funding, etc. So even if there was a single EU rule book or 28th regime, without a single market regulator, there would be divergence and patchwork in implementation and enforcement.
